title: Chapter 62
content:
When Jakyeong finally opened his eyes, the bedroom was plunged in midnight shadow. Groping across the nightstand to check the clock, he realized it was already past noon. He hit the wall switch, and the electric blinds glided upward, flooding the suite with brilliant midday sunlight.

Wincing through a swollen, heavy-lidded glare, he pushed himself up.

A sharp, shooting ache flared from his tailbone straight up his spine, wrenching an involuntary groan from his throat. Kang Il-hyun had kept him pinned in a suffocating embrace from behind well into the early hours of dawn, but the man had already vanished for work. Staring at the rumpled, empty side of the mattress, Jakyeong swung his legs over the edge. Discarded clothes lay strewn across the hardwood, flanked by a damp towel on the nightstand.

He padded into the en-suite bath, putting a cigarette between his lips. Flicking his lighter, he caught his reflection in the vanity mirror and froze.

Not a single patch of skin had been spared.

He let out a hollow, incredulous laugh, twisting around to inspect his back. To an outsider, he looked like a quarantined plague patient. The dark, mottled love bites didn't stop at his torso—they trailed up his throat to the underside of his jawline, paired with faint, distinct teeth indentations along his cheek.

That psychotic bastard. Why didn't you just carve off a piece and chew it whole?

Grinding his teeth, he sparked the flame, dragging the smoke deep into his lungs before stepping back into the bedroom. A towering stack of medicated pain-relief patches sat on the coffee table where Il-hyun had left them the night before. Did the bastard stockpile these because he knew he was going to tear me apart like this?

He peeled the backing off the patches, slapping them across his neck to conceal the bruised patchwork. After snubbing out the cigarette, he pulled on fresh clothes and stepped into the hallway.

He rapped his knuckles against the door of the adjoining suite. Dead silence.

Heading down the grand staircase, lively chatter drifted from the dining room.

Wang Han and Wang Ryun were seated at the table, deep in conversation with the senior housekeeper.

Catching sight of Jakyeong first, she greeted him with a warm, maternal smile. "You're awake?"

Han and Ryun turned around in unison.

"Look who finally decided to join the living," Ryun called out. "Come grab some lunch. The housekeeper made this spread, and it's incredible."

The two looked entirely at home, lounging as if they owned the estate. Jakyeong kept his face completely blank, pulling out a chair opposite them.

Ryun leaned forward across the mahogany table, lowering his voice with a smirk. "You holding up alright?"

Jakyeong met his eyes. "What's that supposed to mean?"

"Need me to fetch a soft cushion for your chair? Want to sit on something plush?"

Jakyeong scowled, but before he could fire back, Han drove a hard, punitive elbow into Ryun’s ribs. Ryun choked on his food, desperately fighting back a laugh as his cheeks twitched.

Jakyeong clamped his jaw shut, glaring at his brother. Fuck. They heard everything.

He knew he would never hear the end of this for the next century. Han was one thing, but Ryun was relentless. Back when they were kids, Jakyeong had once pissed his pants after being chased down by a stray dog, and Ryun had weaponized the story for three straight years.

Grinding his molars, Jakyeong directed every ounce of silent venom toward Kang Il-hyun. Who else is there to blame? I should have kicked him out the door, but the second he went down on me, I completely lost my goddamn mind.

Finishing lunch, the trio relocated outside, settling into a row of teak chairs by the pool deck. A server approached offering iced tea, but they politely declined. After scanning the perimeter for physical bugs, Jakyeong lit a cigarette. Private security guards patrolled the grounds, but they kept a respectful distance, granting the guests operational privacy.

Instead, the estate was blanketed by a dense grid of rotating CCTV domes overhead. Deciding there was zero point in acting paranoid, they reclined comfortably in the shade.

"Have you made up your mind?" Han asked quietly.

Ryun let out a snort. "You really think he had the mental bandwidth to think about business last night?"

"Ryun-ge. Shut your mouth."

"Don't tell me those teeth marks on your cheek are from President Kang too? Man's as wild in bed as he is in the boardroom, huh?"

Jakyeong narrowed his eyes, pulling hard on his cigarette. "Keep running your mouth and I'll put a bullet through it."

Han cut in, scolding them both. "Knock it off. This isn't the time for cheap jokes."

Ryun raised his heavily bandaged right hand, waving the reattached pinky. "I vote yes. One year is nothing in this line of work. I'm sick of living like a fugitive out of duffel bags anyway, and the money is absurdly good."

Han’s gaze shifted to Jakyeong.

Jakyeong took a slow, measured drag, staring into the middle distance before speaking in a low, even tone.

"I vote yes too. For now."

Refusing the deal wasn't a realistic play; Kang Il-hyun would stop at nothing to drag his signature onto that paper—even if it meant severing a hand and pressing his bloody thumbprint onto the line. The man was thoroughly capable of it.

Jakyeong checked the tree line, ensuring no guards were within earshot, and dropped his voice to a whisper:

"We take the deal... and we breach the contract halfway through."

Han blinked. "What are you talking about?"

"I'm saying we take the upfront cash and cut our losses."

Both brothers stared in disbelief.

"Wait," Ryun muttered, his eyes widening. "You weren't joking about that yesterday?"

"I was dead serious."

The corners of Ryun’s mouth immediately pulled into a broad, delighted grin. You clever little devil. Ryun moved to grab Jakyeong’s face for an affectionate kiss, but Jakyeong shoved him back by the jaw.

Wang Han, however, remained deeply troubled.

"Is that safe?"

"Do you honestly think Kang Il-hyun plans on letting us walk away clean once the year is up?" Jakyeong countered. "The moment Chairman Kang finds out we're working for his son, he'll put a contract out on our heads too. Surviving twelve months under this roof is impossible. The cleanest play is taking the upfront lump sum, handling a couple of initial cleanups, and disappearing before the net closes."

"Hmm."

"We'll have to go dark for a while, but living off the grid is our specialty."

While Han weighed the options, Jakyeong shot a sharp glare toward Ryun. "And that plan only works if Ryun-ge doesn't go running back to Seoul for some skirt."

Ryun cleared his throat, suddenly finding the pool tiles fascinating. He had slipped into Korea under the radar to meet his girlfriend and make a discreet pilgrimage to the parish shelter, never imagining Il-hyun's network would descend on him so fast. With his share of the advance, his plan was to purchase fresh foreign identities and relocate with her to Norway or New Zealand to live out their days in clean air.

As the team's anchor, Wang Han struggled to give the final nod.

Betrayal was standard currency in the underworld, yet Jakyeong had always operated on a strict, personal code of professional honor. The kid had always preached that credibility came first—yet this would mark the second time he planned to put a bullet through Kang Il-hyun’s operations.

Though in fairness, Il-hyun had fired the first shot by issuing a kill order at the inauguration.

Han let out a heavy sigh, unable to give an immediate verdict. Leading this cell meant carrying the weight of their lives; if this scheme went sideways, Kang Il-hyun wouldn't hesitate to butcher all three of them on the spot.

Perched in his leather armchair with a lit cigar between his teeth, Chairman Kang reviewed the thick dossier Il-hyun had placed on his desk.

It was a comprehensive feasibility report for a multi-billion-won integrated luxury resort and commercial complex on Jeju Island. The execution was remarkably thorough, but the success of the project posed a dangerous dilemma: cementing Il-hyun’s corporate standing would only swell the ranks of board members rallying behind him—especially while Kang Tae-han continued to show zero tangible results.

"It looks... acceptable."

Il-hyun offered a faint, thin smirk.

He knew better than anyone that the old man was seething behind that measured tone. Ever since the botched hit twelve months ago, the patriarch had treated Il-hyun with sickening, grandfatherly warmth. Il-hyun had mirrored the act flawlessly.

Though Il-hyun possessed the black-market USB drive Jakyeong had provided, the file contained undeniable evidence of his own treasonous plots against his father. They were back at square one: two predators locked in an uneasy stalemate, waiting for the other to expose his throat while playing the dutiful father and son.

"However... given the fierce resistance from several founding directors, we should table the rollout for the time being."

Naturally, Il-hyun mused, giving an easy, agreeable nod. The board wasn't resisting on its own accord—they were dancing on Chairman Kang's strings. Yet even as a fading relic, the old man’s institutional grip on voting shares was a formidable obstacle.

Whispers were already circulating that an extraordinary shareholder assembly would be convened soon to officially designate the corporate successor. If the vote went to the floor, Chairman Kang’s majority bloc held the upper hand.

Il-hyun masked his cold amusement behind a placid face, sipping his tea. The bitter, steeped brew matched the venom in his gut.

Concluding the briefing, Il-hyun descended to his private executive suite.

The moment the heavy mahogany doors clicked shut, he used the remote to switch on the wall monitor. The screen partitioned into high-definition security feeds covering every inch of his private estate.

Lee Ja-kyeong was currently gathered by the pool deck with the two Wang brothers.

Il-hyun maximized the feed. Park Tae-soo stepped into the office, his eyes lingering on the display.

"Shall I engage the audio intercept, President Kang?"

Il-hyun slid a cigarette between his lips, a slow smirk spreading across his face. "Leave it. At best, they're scheming some half-baked plan to take the cash and skip the country."

He sparked the flame, drawing a massive lungful of smoke until his cheeks hollowed, before releasing a thick gray cloud.

Through the screen, Ja-kyeong’s face wasn't entirely clear, but the boy looked loose and animated. Beside the desk, Tae-soo’s expression was uncharacteristically dark. Il-hyun knew exactly what was eating at his security chief—the operative had already put two high-caliber rounds through his legs; turning a gun on him a second time wouldn't be a stretch.

"Anxious, Tae-soo?"

"Not at all, sir."

"Ja-kyeong doesn't trust me anyway," Il-hyun said smoothly. "Our only move is to play along with his little games and keep him pampered on a long leash."

Whether he wanted to keep the boy out of raw possessiveness or because teasing the little stray was the only entertainment that kept him sane, Il-hyun hadn't fully decided. But he knew with absolute certainty that this fixation wasn't something that would burn out anytime soon.

The trouble was that Lee Ja-kyeong felt zero genuine affection toward him. To the kid, Il-hyun was merely a conduit for physical release—a very expensive, living sex toy. The realization left a bitter taste in his mouth, far foulier than the tea he’d shared with his father.

On the monitor, the three operatives rose to their feet in unison.

Ryun must have dropped another lewd comment, because Jakyeong suddenly drove a vicious punch into the man's shoulder. In the next breath, Jakyeong clamped a hand over his own lower back, hunching over with a visible wince.

Even without audio, Il-hyun could practically hear the stream of colorful curses pouring from the boy's mouth.

A broad, predatory grin spread across Il-hyun’s bruised lips.

"Looks like they've reached a verdict."

"Yes, sir."

"Compile Choi Man-sik’s biographical profile, personal security routines, and daily itineraries. Deliver the file to the estate tonight. Tell them to initiate surveillance immediately."

Tae-soo bowed. "Understood, President Kang."

Il-hyun crushed out the cigarette in the crystal tray, leaning back into the leather sofa. The monitor tracked Ja-kyeong’s movements as he crossed the lawn. Surrounded by his brothers, the boy looked undeniably at ease—yet every few strides, his hand drifted down to rub at his aching lower back.

Did I push him too hard last night?

The fleeting pang of remorse lasted less than a second. Watching the boy wince only brought the memory of that flushed, wrecked face back into focus, sending a heavy, throbbing heat pooling straight to his groin.
